parts.t: Hazelmere is a rural community on the southeast side of Surrey, east of White Rock and Semiahmoo Bay. The Little Campbell River winds through it toward Boundary Bay, and much of its watershed is farmland in the Agricultural Land Reserve. A 1903 church, a cemetery the community ran itself for 50 years and an old Hall’s Prairie school building still mark the farm community that grew up here. With wells, septic systems and ALR rules in play, the land and its paperwork come before the house.

No City land use plan is named for Hazelmere, so zoning and ALR status for the exact parcel are what count.
The City’s South Surrey land use plans page lists no plan for Hazelmere.
A large part of the Little Campbell River watershed is in the Agricultural Land Reserve, where Agricultural Land Commission rules apply on top of City zoning.
To the north-east, the South Campbell Heights Local Area Plan covers about 249 hectares south of Campbell Heights Business Park. It does not name Hazelmere.
Hazelmere United Church, Hazelmere Cemetery and the Hall’s Prairie South Building are on the City’s heritage site list.
Find out whether any part of the parcel is in the reserve before you plan anything else.
Order a flow and potability test during the subject period, and ask the seller for older results.
A pump-out and inspection shows the tank and field condition. Ask when it was installed.
Compare the barns, shop, arena and any second dwelling with the City’s permit records.
Covenants, rights of way and easements can limit use, and a shared driveway needs a written agreement.
Tributaries of the Little Campbell River cross the area, and streamside setbacks can limit where you build.

Does the Little Campbell River flood?
Its floodplain closely follows the river channel and is not as wide as Surrey’s other river floodplains, and no dykes have been built on it. Ask the City about the exact property.
